messages.subject: Re: About multiple reactive plots
parts:
What is searchNoun? Is that supposed to be input$searchNoun?

In general, "normal" global variables that are overwritten from reactive functions is a bad "code smell"--i.e., it's not that it's *never* the right answer, but it's almost always a sign that something is wrong. (Global variables that are defined once during startup and just read from reactive functions is fine, though.)

The reason it's a bad code smell is because when you overwrite a normal global variable, reactive functions that read that global variable don't know that anything has changed. The way you generally want to do this instead is to define a reactive function for the variable:

# This appears inside the shinyServer(function(input, output) { ... }) block.
wordcount <- reactive(function() {
  table(input$searchNoun)  # I have no idea what your logic looks like... but make the word count here
})

And then, from both of your reactive plots, call "wordcount()" when you want to access this value. This ensures that when the inputs that affect wordcount change, the reactive plots will know to re-execute themselves.

In case you haven't studied the tutorial chapter on reactivity, here it is:
http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity

We owe you guys a more in-depth description of reactivity as well, once things slow down a little bit for us (ha!) I look forward to getting that going. Thanks for your patience and please ask more questions if things are unclear.
